voices.note: the opening mishnah of Shabbat (2a): the poor man extends his hand; its lemma is cited at 4a.10
the Sages opposing R' Akiva (4a.11) and Rabbi (4b.6, 4b.9) in the cited sources
link in Rav's chain (5a.2) and author of the basket okimta (5a.5)
כי אתא רבין (5a.12), transmitting R' Yochanan
R' Ilai (Elai), the link between R' Avin and R' Yochanan
the mishnah of the scroll rolling from the roof, quoted at 5b.1 as the place Rava's ruling was said
the anonymous first clause of the tevul-yom mishnah quoted at 5b.5
מדאמר מר (5b.7): the four-amot baraita on stopping to rest or to adjust

props.gloss_en: the mishnah: the poor man standing outside extends his hand inside and puts an object into the householder's hand, or takes one from it and carries it out -- the poor man is liable
we require lifting and placing from and onto a place four by four [handbreadths]
Rabba: whose is the mishnah? R' Akiva's, who says we do not require a place four by four
the mishnah (דתנן): one who throws from a private domain to a private domain with the public domain between -- R' Akiva holds him liable
...and the Sages exempt him
R' Akiva holds: an object caught in the airspace counts as if it were set down
the Rabbis hold: we do not say an object in the airspace counts as set down
dilemma, side 1: they dispute below ten handbreadths, over whether an object in the airspace counts as set down; above ten all exempt, and all agree we do not derive throwing from passing
dilemma, side 2: they dispute above ten handbreadths, over whether throwing is derived from passing; below ten all agree he is liable, since kelutah counts as set down
Rav Yosef: whose is the mishnah? Rabbi's
the baraita: one threw and it came to rest on a projection of any size -- Rabbi holds him liable
...and the Sages exempt him
Abaye: the ziz baraita speaks of a tree standing in a private domain whose boughs lean into the public domain, and the object came to rest on its boughs
Rabbi holds: we cast the boughs after the trunk
the Rabbis hold: we do not cast the boughs after the trunk
the baraita: one threw from the public domain to the public domain with a private domain between -- Rabbi holds him liable
...and the Sages exempt him
Rabbi would obligate him two [sin-offerings]: one for carrying out and one for carrying in
Rav and Shmuel: Rabbi holds him liable only in a roofed private domain, for we say a house is as if full; in an unroofed one, not
(entertained) our mishnah too speaks of a roofed domain
Rav: one who carries an object four cubits in a roofed public domain is exempt, for it is unlike the banners of the desert
R' Zeira: whose is the mishnah? Acherim's
the baraita: Acherim say: if [the receiver] stood in his place and received, [the thrower] is liable; if he moved from his place and received, exempt
R' Abba: our mishnah is where he received in a basket and placed on a basket
R' Yosei b. R' Yehuda: one who fixed a reed in the public domain with a basket on top, and threw and it came to rest on it -- liable [the basket is a private domain]
R' Abbahu: where [the poor man] lowered his hand below three handbreadths and received it
a person's hand counts for him as four by four
one who threw an object and it came to rest in another's hand is liable
the hand counts as four by four even where its owner did not himself deem it a place
if [the receiver] stood in his place and received, [the thrower] is liable
if he moved from his place and received, [the thrower] is exempt
R' Yochanan's dilemma: one threw an object, moved from his place and caught it himself -- what is the law?
Rav Adda bar Ahava: the dilemma is two forces in one person -- like one person (liable), or like two people (exempt)?
one who put his hand into another's courtyard, received rainwater and carried it out is liable
R' Chiyya b. Rav Huna: where he caught it from atop the wall
the mishnah: one reading on the roof whose scroll rolled from his hand -- once it reached ten handbreadths [of the public domain] he turns it over onto its writing [and may not roll it back]
Rava: [the scroll mishnah speaks of] a sloped wall [on which the scroll rests]
Rava: where he caught [the rainwater] from atop a pit [of water]
Rava: water on top of water -- that is its resting
Rava: a nut on water -- that is not its resting
Rava's dilemma: a nut in a vessel floating on water -- do we follow the nut (at rest) or the vessel (moving)?
oil floating on wine [is it resting, for lifting?] is the dispute of R' Yochanan ben Nuri and the Rabbis
the mishnah: oil floating on wine that a tevul yom touched -- he disqualified only the oil
R' Yochanan ben Nuri: the two are joined to each other
one laden with food and drink who goes in and out all day is not liable until he stands still
Abaye: provided he stood [still] to rest
the baraita: within four cubits, if he stopped to rest -- exempt, to adjust the load -- liable; beyond four cubits, to rest -- liable, to adjust -- exempt
one who moved objects from corner to corner, then changed his mind and carried them out, is exempt, for the lifting was not from the outset for this

questions.gloss_en: R' Yochanan: one threw, moved from his place and caught it himself -- are two forces in one person like one person (liable) or like two (exempt)? It stands unresolved
Rava: lifting a nut from a vessel floating on water -- follow the nut (at rest) or the vessel (moving)? It stands unresolved

supports.gloss_en: דתנן: הזורק מרשות היחיד לרשות היחיד ורשות הרבים באמצע, רבי עקיבא מחייב -- the airspace, no four-by-four place, suffices for him
הי רבי? אילימא הא רבי, דתניא: זרק ונח על גבי זיז כל שהוא -- רבי מחייב

deflected_by.gloss_en: התם כדבעינן למימר לקמן כדאביי -- a tree whose trunk is in a private domain; the boughs follow the trunk, a four-by-four place (p_abaye_ilan_nofo)

supports.gloss_en: אלא הא רבי, דתניא: זרק מרשות הרבים לרשות הרבים ורשות היחיד באמצע -- רבי מחייב; ואמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: מחייב היה רבי שתים... אלמא לא בעי עקירה ולא הנחה על גבי מקום ארבעה

deflected_by.gloss_en: הא איתמר עלה, רב ושמואל: לא מחייב רבי אלא ברשות היחיד מקורה (p_rabbi_rak_bimkoreh) -- the roofed house is as if full. The rescue וכי תימא הכא נמי במקורה is felled by Rav's roofed-public-domain ruling (h_bimkoreh, obj_rhr_mekoreh), so this deflection stands

supports.gloss_en: עמד במקומו וקבל חייב, הא בעינן הנחה על גבי מקום ארבעה וליכא! אלא שמע מינה לא בעינן מקום ארבעה
תניא נמי הכי, אחרים אומרים: עמד במקומו וקיבל חייב, עקר ממקומו וקיבל פטור
ואזדא רבא לטעמיה, דאמר רבא: מים על גבי מים היינו הנחתן
ממאי? מדאמר מר: תוך ארבע אמות עמד לפוש פטור, לכתף חייב... -- only stopping to rest is a placing

objections.gloss_en: אמאי חייב? והא בעינן עקירה והנחה מעל גבי מקום ארבעה על ארבעה, וליכא -- a hand is no four-by-four place

answered_by.gloss_en: ידו של אדם חשובה לו כארבעה על ארבעה (= p_yad_chashuva); the five earlier answers are each encoded with the objection that fells it

objections.gloss_en: למימרא דפשיטא ליה לרבה דבקלוטה... ובתוך עשרה פליגי? והא מיבעיא בעי לה רבה -- Rabba's attribution presupposes the kelutah reading of R' Akiva, which he himself raised as a dilemma (4b.1-2)

answered_by.gloss_en: הא לא קשיא: בתר דאיבעיא הדר איפשיטא ליה דסבר רבי עקיבא קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא

objections.gloss_en: ודילמא הנחה הוא דלא בעיא, הא עקירה בעיא -- R' Akiva's view shows only that PLACING needs no four-by-four; lifting may still need one. Unanswered: אלא אמר רב יוסף
התינח ברשות היחיד מקורה, ברשות הרבים מקורה מי חייב? והאמר רב... פטור, לפי שאינו דומה לדגלי מדבר -- the poor man stands in the public domain, and a roofed public domain carries no liability

ודילמא הנחה הוא דלא בעינן, הא עקירה בעינן; והנחה נמי, דילמא דפשיט כנפיה וקבלה -- Acherim may exempt placing only, and even placing may be onto his spread garment. Unanswered: the text moves to R' Abba
והא ידו קתני? -- the mishnah says 'his hand', not a basket

answered_by.gloss_en: תני טרסקל שבידו -- read 'the basket in his hand'

objections.gloss_en: התינח טרסקל ברשות היחיד, אלא טרסקל שברשות הרבים רשות היחיד הוא -- לימא דלא כרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: on his view the householder handing into the poor man's basket moves private to private; why liable?

answered_by.gloss_en: אפילו תימא רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: התם למעלה מעשרה, הכא למטה מעשרה -- a basket below ten is not a private domain

objections.gloss_en: קשיא ליה לרבי אבהו: מי קתני טרסקל שבידו? והא ידו קתני! -- he rejects the emendation that answered obj_yado_katani (an objection cannot target an answer; see header). Unanswered: אלא אמר רבי אבהו
והא עומד קתני? -- the mishnah has the poor man standing; how is his hand within three of the ground?

answered_by.gloss_en: ואיבעית אימא בגומא -- he stands in a pit
ואיבעית אימא בננס -- he is a dwarf

objections.gloss_en: איכפל תנא לאשמועינן כל הני?! -- would the tanna have gone to such lengths to teach us these cases? Unanswered: אלא אמר רבא
מתקיף לה רבי זירא: מה לי הטעינו חבירו, מה לי הטעינו שמים -- איהו לא עביד עקירה! -- laden by heaven as by his fellow, he performed no lifting

answered_by.gloss_en: לא תימא קיבל אלא קלט -- he actively caught it, which is lifting

objections.gloss_en: והא בעינן עקירה מעל גבי מקום ארבעה, וליכא -- rain in the air is lifted from no four-by-four place

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא אמר רבא: כגון שקלט מעל גבי גומא (= p_rava_gumma); R' Chiyya b. Rav Huna's wall (5a.18) falls on the way -- see obj_ha_lo_nach and obj_mayim_lo_nayechi

objections.gloss_en: על גבי כותל נמי, והא לא נח! -- rain on a wall does not come to rest there

answered_by.gloss_en: כדאמר רבא בכותל משופע, הכא נמי בכותל משופע -- a sloped wall, as Rava said of the scroll (p_rava_kotel_meshupa)

objections.gloss_en: אימור דאמר רבא בספר, דעביד דנייח; מים מי עבידי דנייחי?! -- a scroll rests on a slope, water does not; this knocks down a_kotel_meshupa (targeted at the okimta it rescued -- see header). Unanswered: אלא אמר רבא
והוינן בה: אמאי הופכו על הכתב? הא לא נח! -- the scroll has not come to rest in the public domain, so rolling it back would be no lifting

answered_by.gloss_en: ואמר רבא: בכותל משופע -- the scroll rests on a sloped wall (= p_rava_kotel_meshupa)
